title: Water Flowing from the Temple and the Land Borders

questions.question: Where did Ezekiel see the water issuing from?
options: From below the threshold of the temple toward the east
From a crack in the Mount of Olives
From the roof of the temple
From a rock in the wilderness
questions.correctAnswer: From below the threshold of the temple toward the east
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 47:1 (ESV): "Then he brought me back to the door of the temple, and behold, water was issuing from below the threshold of the temple toward the east..."

questions.question: Which side of the altar did the water flow down?
options: The south side
The north side
The east side
The west side
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 47:1 (ESV): "The water was flowing down from below the south end of the threshold of the temple, south of the altar."

questions.question: The man led Ezekiel east and measured 1,000 cubits, passing him through the water. How deep was the water the first time?
options: Ankle-deep
Knee-deep
Waist-deep
Too deep to pass, a river to swim in
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 47:3 (ESV): "Going on eastward with a measuring line in his hand, the man measured a thousand cubits, and then led me through the water, and it was ankle-deep."

questions.question: He measured another thousand cubits. How deep was the water then?
options: Knee-deep
Ankle-deep
Waist-deep
To the neck
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 47:4 (ESV): "Again he measured a thousand, and led me through the water, and it was knee-deep."

questions.question: He measured another thousand cubits. How deep was the water the third time?
options: Waist-deep
Knee-deep
Over his head
Dry land
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 47:4 (ESV): "Again he measured a thousand, and led me through the water, and it was waist-deep."

questions.question: He measured a fourth thousand cubits. What had the water become?
options: A river that could not be passed through, deep enough to swim in
A stagnant pool
A raging waterfall
A sea of glass
questions.correctAnswer: A river that could not be passed through, deep enough to swim in
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 47:5 (ESV): "Again he measured a thousand, and it was a river that I could not pass through, for the water had risen. It was deep enough to swim in, a river that could not be passed through."

questions.question: When the man brought Ezekiel back along the bank of the river, what did he see?
options: Very many trees on the one side and on the other
Ruins of ancient cities
Bones of those who died in the exile
Statues of gold
questions.correctAnswer: Very many trees on the one side and on the other
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 47:7 (ESV): "As I went back, I saw on the bank of the river very many trees on the one side and on the other."

questions.question: Where do these temple waters flow, and what do they heal?
options: They flow down into the Arabah and enter the sea [the Dead Sea]; its water will become fresh/healed
They flow into the Great Sea (Mediterranean) and part it
They flow into Egypt to heal the plagues
They flow into Babylon to destroy it
questions.correctAnswer: They flow down into the Arabah and enter the sea [the Dead Sea]; its water will become fresh/healed
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 47:8 (ESV): "...This water flows toward the eastern region and goes down into the Arabah, and enters the sea; when the water flows into the sea, the water will become fresh."

questions.question: What happens wherever the river goes?
options: Every living creature that swarms will live, and there will be very many fish
All the fish die and float to the surface
The ground turns to brass
Only briars and thorns grow
questions.correctAnswer: Every living creature that swarms will live, and there will be very many fish
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 47:9 (ESV): "And wherever the river goes, every living creature that swarms will live, and there will be very many fish. For this water goes there, that the waters of the sea may become fresh; so everything will live where the river goes."

questions.question: What will the fishermen do beside the newly healed sea from Engedi to Eneglaim?
options: It will be a place for the spreading of nets, and their fish will be of very many kinds, like the fish of the Great Sea
They will catch nothing, for the sea is cursed
They will fish for pearls instead
They will build altars to the fish gods
questions.correctAnswer: It will be a place for the spreading of nets, and their fish will be of very many kinds, like the fish of the Great Sea
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 47:10 (ESV): "Fishermen will stand beside the sea. From Engedi to Eneglaim it will be a place for the spreading of nets. Its fish will be of very many kinds, like the fish of the Great Sea."

questions.question: What will NOT become fresh, but will be left for salt?
options: Its swamps and marshes
The rivers of Babylon
The Sea of Galilee
The wells of Beersheba
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 47:11 (ESV): "But its swamps and marshes will not become fresh; they are to be left for salt."

questions.question: What is special about the trees that grow on both banks of this river?
options: Their leaves will not wither, nor their fruit fail, but they will bear fresh fruit every month. Their fruit will be for food, and their leaves for healing
They are golden trees that produce gems
They will only produce fruit once every fifty years
Their fruit is poisonous but their leaves are sweet
questions.correctAnswer: Their leaves will not wither, nor their fruit fail, but they will bear fresh fruit every month. Their fruit will be for food, and their leaves for healing
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 47:12 (ESV): "And on the banks, on both sides of the river, there will grow all kinds of trees for food. Their leaves will not wither, nor their fruit fail, but they will bear fresh fruit every month, because the water for them flows from the sanctuary. Their fruit will be for food, and their leaves for healing."

questions.question: God then gives the boundaries of the land to be inherited by the twelve tribes. Which tribe gets two portions?
options: Joseph
Judah
Levi
Benjamin
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 47:13 (ESV): "...The boundary rules by which you shall apportion the land for inheritance among the twelve tribes of Israel. Joseph shall have two portions." (Manasseh and Ephraim).

questions.question: Against what other nation is Israel to divide the land "equally with one another" because God swore to give it to their fathers?
options: There are no nations, they inherit it evenly among themselves
They share it evenly with the Edomites
They divide it with the Egyptians
They give half to the remnants of Canaan
questions.correctAnswer: There are no nations, they inherit it evenly among themselves
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 47:14 (ESV): "And you shall divide it equally with one another, for I swore to give it to your fathers, and this land shall fall to you as your inheritance."

questions.question: What does God command concerning the sojourners (aliens/foreigners) who reside among them and have had children among them?
options: "They shall be to you as native-born children of Israel. With you they shall be allotted an inheritance among the tribes of Israel."
"They must be expelled before the Jubilee."
"They shall serve as slaves in the temple."
"They may live there, but cannot own land."
questions.correctAnswer: "They shall be to you as native-born children of Israel. With you they shall be allotted an inheritance among the tribes of Israel."
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 47:22 (ESV): "You shall allot it as an inheritance for yourselves and for the sojourners who reside among you and have had children among you. They shall be to you as native-born children of Israel. With you they shall be allotted an inheritance among the tribes of Israel."

key_verse_text: "And on the banks, on both sides of the river, there will grow all kinds of trees for food. Their leaves will not wither, nor their fruit fail, but they will bear fresh fruit every month, because the water for them flows from the sanctuary. Their fruit will be for food, and their leaves for healing."
